spec_desc:
- Entry signal: Donchian channel breakout. Bullish whenever the close is strictly above the highest high of the 48 bars before the current bar; bearish whenever the close is strictly below the lowest low of those 48 bars. This is a level condition, true on every bar it holds.
- Direction: long and short (a bullish signal opens a long when flat, a bearish one opens a short when flat).
- Trend filter on completed 60-minute candles: only take long entries when the last completed 60-minute close is strictly above the 20-period EMA of those candles' closes, and only take short entries when it is strictly below. The filter only blocks entries, never exits.
- Position size: volatility-scaled. Fraction of equity = 0.01 x close / (1 x ATR(14)) on the signal bar, capped at 1.0 and floored at 0.05.
- Time stop: if the trade is still open 128 bars after the signal bar, exit at the next open (decide on the bar where bars-since-signal reaches 128).
- Trailing stop: track the best price of the trade (highest high for longs, lowest low for shorts, starting from the entry price and updated with each bar's high/low while the position is held); the stop sits 1.5 x entry ATR behind that extreme.
- A signal in the opposite direction of an open trade closes it at the next open.

If we hit 32 bars since the signal bar, bail at the next open. Also, if an opposite signal prints, flip the position at the next open, simple as that.

spec_desc:
- Entry signal: Donchian channel breakout. Bullish whenever the close is strictly above the highest high of the 96 bars before the current bar; bearish whenever the close is strictly below the lowest low of those 96 bars. This is a level condition, true on every bar it holds.
- Direction: long and short (a bullish signal opens a long when flat, a bearish one opens a short when flat).
- Position size: start with 0.25 of equity, then pyramid. While in the trade, each time the close is at least 2 x the entry ATR beyond the price of the last add (initially the entry price) in the trade's favour, add another 0.25 (total capped at 1.0), at most 2 add(s) per trade; the add price becomes that bar's close.
- Time stop: if the trade is still open 32 bars after the signal bar, exit at the next open (decide on the bar where bars-since-signal reaches 32).
- A signal in the opposite direction of an open trade closes it at the next open.

attempts.text: Trade the 15 using a breakout retest setup. When price closes above the 48-bar high, it arms a bull setup for 32 bars to buy the retest when a candle low hits that level, with new breaks resetting the clock, and mirror for bears. Go long or get short when flat, sizing in at 0.5% times close over 1 ATR with an r of 1 and k of 1, floored at 5% and capped at 100%. Bank half when a candle closes at least 3 ATRs in the green, letting the runner ride. Exit at the open after 128 bars or flip on an opposite signal.

spec_desc:
- Entry signal: breakout then retest. When the close is strictly above the highest high of the 48 bars before the current bar, remember that high as the breakout level (a newer breakout replaces the old one and restarts the clock). The setup stays armed for 32 bars after the breakout bar. While armed, the first bar whose low trades at or below the level is the bullish signal and disarms the setup; if more than 32 bars pass first, the setup simply expires. The bearish version is the mirror image (close below the 48-bar lowest low, then a high at or above that level). Arming, expiry and triggering are checked on every bar, in or out of a position; a newer breakout in either direction replaces the armed setup.
- Direction: long and short (a bullish signal opens a long when flat, a bearish one opens a short when flat).
- Position size: volatility-scaled. Fraction of equity = 0.005 x close / (1 x ATR(14)) on the signal bar, capped at 1.0 and floored at 0.05.
- Scale out: the first time a bar closes at least 3 x entry ATR in profit, cut the position to half its current size (once per trade); the rest stays on.
- Time stop: if the trade is still open 128 bars after the signal bar, exit at the next open (decide on the bar where bars-since-signal reaches 128).
- A signal in the opposite direction of an open trade closes it at the next open.

Once in, update the extreme high and trail your stop 2 times the entry ATR behind it. Cut it if we hit a 256-bar time stop, or flip short on any breakdown signal which just flattens us.

spec_desc:
- Entry signal: range-box breakout. The box is the highest high and lowest low of the 64 bars before the current bar. It only counts as a box if its height (top minus bottom) is at most 6 times the current ATR(14). Bullish when the close is strictly above the top of a valid box; bearish when the close is strictly below its bottom.
- Direction: long only (bearish signals only close longs).
- Position size: volatility-scaled. Fraction of equity = 0.01 x close / (3 x ATR(14)) on the signal bar, capped at 1.0 and floored at 0.05.
- Time stop: if the trade is still open 256 bars after the signal bar, exit at the next open (decide on the bar where bars-since-signal reaches 256).
- Trailing stop: track the best price of the trade (highest high for longs, lowest low for shorts, starting from the entry price and updated with each bar's high/low while the position is held); the stop sits 2 x entry ATR behind that extreme.
- A signal in the opposite direction of an open trade closes it at the next open.

spec_desc:
- Entry signal: Donchian channel breakout. Bullish whenever the close is strictly above the highest high of the 96 bars before the current bar; bearish whenever the close is strictly below the lowest low of those 96 bars. This is a level condition, true on every bar it holds.
- Direction: long and short (a bullish signal opens a long when flat, a bearish one opens a short when flat).
- Trend filter on completed 240-minute candles: only take long entries when the last completed 240-minute close is strictly above the 50-period EMA of those candles' closes, and only take short entries when it is strictly below. The filter only blocks entries, never exits.
- Position size: volatility-scaled. Fraction of equity = 0.005 x close / (3 x ATR(14)) on the signal bar, capped at 1.0 and floored at 0.05.
- Moving box: the trade lives in a box anchored at the entry price, with the stop 1 x entry ATR behind the anchor and the target 2 x entry ATR beyond it. Every time a bar closes at least another 2 x entry ATR in profit beyond the current anchor, shift the whole box (anchor, stop and target) 2 x entry ATR in the trade's favour (repeat if the close cleared several steps). The box never shifts back.
- Breakeven: once a bar closes at least 0.5 x entry ATR in profit, move the stop to the entry price for the rest of the trade (it never moves back).
- Cooldown: after any trade ends, take no new entry for 96 bars, counted from the bar on which you first see yourself flat (entries allowed again from that bar + 96).
- A signal in the opposite direction of an open trade closes it at the next open.

attempts.text: Let's code a vol-scaled 14 RSI mean reversion system on the 15. Go long when RSI crosses back up through 30, and flip short when it crosses back down through 70, while flat. Use a 1h trend filter with a 20 EMA. Size in at 0.5% equity times close over 3 times the entry 14 ATR, capped at 1.0 and floored at 0.05. Use a trailing box: stop 1 ATR behind, target 3 ATR ahead, ratcheting the box 1 ATR every time a bar closes at least 1 ATR further in the green. An opposite signal gets flat. Max 3 entries a day, with a 4-hour cooldown.

spec_desc:
- Entry signal: RSI(14) mean reversion. Bullish when RSI crosses back up through 30 (below 30 on the previous bar, at or above 30 now); bearish when it crosses back down through 100-30 (above it on the previous bar, at or below it now).
- Direction: long and short (a bullish signal opens a long when flat, a bearish one opens a short when flat).
- Trend filter on completed 60-minute candles: only take long entries when the last completed 60-minute close is strictly above the 20-period EMA of those candles' closes, and only take short entries when it is strictly below. The filter only blocks entries, never exits.
- Position size: volatility-scaled. Fraction of equity = 0.005 x close / (3 x ATR(14)) on the signal bar, capped at 1.0 and floored at 0.05.
- Moving box: the trade lives in a box anchored at the entry price, with the stop 1 x entry ATR behind the anchor and the target 3 x entry ATR beyond it. Every time a bar closes at least another 1 x entry ATR in profit beyond the current anchor, shift the whole box (anchor, stop and target) 1 x entry ATR in the trade's favour (repeat if the close cleared several steps). The box never shifts back.
- Cooldown: after any trade ends, take no new entry for 16 bars, counted from the bar on which you first see yourself flat (entries allowed again from that bar + 16).
- Daily cap: at most 3 new entries per UTC calendar day (by the signal bar's open time); further signals that day are ignored.
- A signal in the opposite direction of an open trade closes it at the next open.

spec_desc:
- Entry signal: Donchian channel breakout. Bullish whenever the close is strictly above the highest high of the 192 bars before the current bar; bearish whenever the close is strictly below the lowest low of those 192 bars. This is a level condition, true on every bar it holds.
- Direction: long only (bearish signals only close longs).
- Position size: volatility-scaled. Fraction of equity = 0.0025 x close / (3 x ATR(14)) on the signal bar, capped at 1.0 and floored at 0.05.
- Protective stop 1 x entry ATR away from the entry price (below for longs, above for shorts).
- Take-profit order 6 x entry ATR beyond the entry price.
- Trailing stop: track the best price of the trade (highest high for longs, lowest low for shorts, starting from the entry price and updated with each bar's high/low while the position is held); the stop sits 3 x entry ATR behind that extreme.
- A signal in the opposite direction of an open trade closes it at the next open.

spec_desc:
- Entry signal: breakout then retest. When the close is strictly above the highest high of the 96 bars before the current bar, remember that high as the breakout level (a newer breakout replaces the old one and restarts the clock). The setup stays armed for 8 bars after the breakout bar. While armed, the first bar whose low trades at or below the level is the bullish signal and disarms the setup; if more than 8 bars pass first, the setup simply expires. The bearish version is the mirror image (close below the 96-bar lowest low, then a high at or above that level). Arming, expiry and triggering are checked on every bar, in or out of a position; a newer breakout in either direction replaces the armed setup.
- Direction: long only (bearish signals only close longs).
- Trend filter on completed 240-minute candles: only take long entries when the last completed 240-minute close is strictly above the 20-period EMA of those candles' closes, and only take short entries when it is strictly below. The filter only blocks entries, never exits.
- Position size: a fixed 0.25 of equity per trade.
- Protective stop 1 x entry ATR away from the entry price (below for longs, above for shorts).
- Trailing stop: track the best price of the trade (highest high for longs, lowest low for shorts, starting from the entry price and updated with each bar's high/low while the position is held); the stop sits 4 x entry ATR behind that extreme.
- A signal in the opposite direction of an open trade closes it at the next open.

Size in volatility-scaled, taking 1 percent of equity times the close divided by 2 times the 14-period ATR, floored at 5 percent and capped at 100 percent. Once in the green, scale out by cutting the position to half size the first time a bar close reaches at least 3 ATR in profit, and let the rest ride into a 4 ATR take-profit order. If we see a signal in the opposite direction, bail and get flat.

spec_desc:
- Entry signal: Donchian channel breakout. Bullish whenever the close is strictly above the highest high of the 96 bars before the current bar; bearish whenever the close is strictly below the lowest low of those 96 bars. This is a level condition, true on every bar it holds.
- Direction: long and short (a bullish signal opens a long when flat, a bearish one opens a short when flat).
- Position size: volatility-scaled. Fraction of equity = 0.01 x close / (2 x ATR(14)) on the signal bar, capped at 1.0 and floored at 0.05.
- Scale out: the first time a bar closes at least 3 x entry ATR in profit, cut the position to half its current size (once per trade); the rest stays on.
- Take-profit order 4 x entry ATR beyond the entry price.
- A signal in the opposite direction of an open trade closes it at the next open.

q: Need a range-box breakout model for the 15. Look at the highest high and lowest low of the prior 32 bars; if that box is no more than 6 times the current ATR, we trade it both ways. Get long if we close above the top, get short if we close below. Size in 1 unit of equity per trade. Put a hard stop 1.5 ATR away from entry. If an opposite signal prints while in a trade, bail. After getting flat, sit on hands for a 16-bar cooldown before taking another setup.

spec_desc:
- Entry signal: range-box breakout. The box is the highest high and lowest low of the 32 bars before the current bar. It only counts as a box if its height (top minus bottom) is at most 6 times the current ATR(14). Bullish when the close is strictly above the top of a valid box; bearish when the close is strictly below its bottom.
- Direction: long and short (a bullish signal opens a long when flat, a bearish one opens a short when flat).
- Position size: a fixed 1 of equity per trade.
- Cooldown: after any trade ends, take no new entry for 16 bars, counted from the bar on which you first see yourself flat (entries allowed again from that bar + 16).
- Protective stop 1.5 x entry ATR away from the entry price (below for longs, above for shorts).
- A signal in the opposite direction of an open trade closes it at the next open.

- Position size: a fixed 1 of equity per trade.
- Scale out: the first time a bar closes at least 3 x entry ATR in profit, cut the position to half its current size (once per trade); the rest stays on.
- Trailing stop: track the best price of the trade (highest high for longs, lowest low for shorts, starting from the entry price and updated with each bar's high/low while the position is held); the stop sits 4 x entry ATR behind that extreme.
- A signal in the opposite direction of an open trade closes it at the next open.

attempts.text: Spin up a Donchian breakout system on the 15 catching both ways. When price breaks the 48-bar high or low, we go long or get short when flat. Check the 1h trend filter first, taking longs only above the 20 EMA and shorts only below. Vol-scale the size using 0.25% of equity times close over ATR 14, capped at 1.0 and floored at 0.05. Once a bar closes at least 1.5 ATRs in profit, scale out and take some off the table, cutting the position to half size, and let the rest ride. An opposite signal closes the trade by getting flat.

spec_desc:
- Entry signal: Donchian channel breakout. Bullish whenever the close is strictly above the highest high of the 48 bars before the current bar; bearish whenever the close is strictly below the lowest low of those 48 bars. This is a level condition, true on every bar it holds.
- Direction: long and short (a bullish signal opens a long when flat, a bearish one opens a short when flat).
- Trend filter on completed 60-minute candles: only take long entries when the last completed 60-minute close is strictly above the 20-period EMA of those candles' closes, and only take short entries when it is strictly below. The filter only blocks entries, never exits.
- Position size: volatility-scaled. Fraction of equity = 0.0025 x close / (1 x ATR(14)) on the signal bar, capped at 1.0 and floored at 0.05.
- Scale out: the first time a bar closes at least 1.5 x entry ATR in profit, cut the position to half its current size (once per trade); the rest stays on.
- A signal in the opposite direction of an open trade closes it at the next open.

Size in at 75% equity both ways. If we get an opposite signal while in a trade, flip out at the next open. After any trade ends, enforce a 4-bar cooldown before taking new entries.

- Breakeven: once a bar closes at least 1 x entry ATR in profit, move the stop to the entry price for the rest of the trade (it never moves back).
